title: Five technology predictions shaping energy and resources in 2027
summary: Agentic AI will transform energy and resources. The question is how quickly companies can connect trusted data and put it to work.
body_markdown:
For technology, operations, project, supply-chain, security, and customer-experience leaders across[utilities](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/utilities) ,[oil and gas](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/oil-and-gas) ,[chemicals](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/chemicals) , and[metals and mining](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/metals-and-mining) , 2027 will mark a turning point. Agentic AI for[Energy and Resources](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/energy-and-resources) will move beyond answering questions to coordinating work and completing defined tasks across complex operations. Agentic AI uses governed software agents to coordinate work and complete defined tasks across enterprise and operational systems, within human-set limits. But AI cannot operate reliably on fragmented, outdated, or unverified information. It needs trusted context and connected data spanning assets, projects, operations, customers, employees, and supply chains. Organizations that build this foundation will be better positioned to manage rising demand, infrastructure constraints, disruption, cyber risk, costs, and customer expectations. These five predictions show where secure information management for agentic AI is heading next.


## **AI agents transform project execution**


In 2027, AI agents will take on more capital-project work, not just answer questions about it. Accenture highlights how AI and automation can streamline contracts, workflows, and reporting, improve project coordination, and identify risks earlier, helping teams execute complex projects more efficiently and predictably.1


This will accelerate[AI-driven project execution](https://www.opentext.com/media/point-of-view/capital-projects-reimagined-for-energy-and-resources-pov-en.pdf) . Construction Work Package Agents, Engineering Change Agents, and Project Handover Agents could help teams coordinate information and work across project stages.


Agents need trusted context connecting drawings, specifications, contracts, schedules, suppliers, equipment, and field information. They must also know which information is current and approved.


[OpenText™ Content Management for Engineering](https://www.opentext.com/products/content-management-for-engineering) and[OpenText™ Documentum™ Content Management for Engineering](https://www.opentext.com/products/documentum-content-management-for-engineering) can provide a governed foundation for document control, reviews,[transmittals, submittals](https://www.opentext.com/media/product-overview/opentext-core-collaboration-for-engineering-po-en.pdf) , changes, collaboration, and handover. Connecting trusted project information with AI can reduce manual effort, reveal issues sooner, and deliver more complete asset information to operations.


## **AI-powered asset operations scale**


In 2027, agentic AI will move deeper into asset operations, connecting maintenance history, engineering information, procedures, sensor data, spare-parts availability, and workforce knowledge. Adoption, however, will depend on trust. Only 13% of energy executives trust AI-generated outputs, according to Deloitte.2


[AI-powered asset operations](https://www.opentext.com/media/point-of-view/reimagining-the-future-of-asset-operations-for-energy-and-resources-pov-en.pdf) can help close that gap by grounding agents in trusted context and connected data. Agents could identify recurring equipment problems, assemble information for maintenance work, locate current procedures, and surface relevant drawings and work histories.


The goal is not to remove people from critical decisions. It is to reduce the information friction surrounding those decisions. When AI understands the relationships among assets, drawings, manuals, maintenance records, inspections, and operating history, organizations can move from generating answers to confidently putting AI to work.


## **Supply chains become agentic networks**


Supply-chain resilience will become more important as Energy and Resources companies navigate concentrated manufacturing, geopolitical risk, equipment shortages, and demand for critical technologies. The IEA warns that geographic concentration across key energy technology supply chains creates vulnerabilities, while stronger and more diverse supply chains can reduce economic-security risks.3


Building[supply-chain resilience](https://www.opentext.com/en/media/point-of-view/supply-chains-reimagined-for-energy-and-resources-pov-en.pdf) requires trusted information across suppliers, procurement, logistics, projects, and operations.[Secure B2B integration](https://www.opentext.com/products/business-network-cloud) can connect suppliers and automate information exchange, while[real-time track and trace](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/shipment-track-and-trace) provides visibility into critical materials, equipment, and shipments from supplier to site.


Agentic AI can build on that connected information. Supply Risk Agents, Transaction Exception Agents, and Materials Traceability Agents could help teams identify issues earlier and respond before disruptions affect maintenance, production, or capital projects.


## **Cybersecurity expands around AI agents**


As AI agents gain access to operational information and business processes, they create new identities, permissions, connections, and potential attack paths. Accenture warns that as AI becomes more integrated into industrial decision-making, increasingly connected operational environments will face expanding cybersecurity risks, requiring greater visibility, threat detection, and protection of critical infrastructure.4


[Cybersecurity for Energy and Resources](https://www.opentext.com/media/point-of-view/cybersecurity-reimagined-for-energy-and-resources-pov-en.pdf) must therefore evolve alongside agentic AI. Organizations will need to understand what an agent can access, which actions it can take, how its behavior is monitored, and when human authorization is required. AI can also strengthen defense by helping security teams investigate threats, prioritize vulnerabilities, detect unusual activity, and accelerate incident response.


For critical infrastructure operators, trustworthy AI will require strong identity controls, least-privilege access, continuous monitoring, human approval gates, and defensible audit trails. Organizations must govern what an AI agent is allowed to know, decide, and do.


## **Utility experiences become proactive**


Utility customer experience will become increasingly connected to affordability, infrastructure investment, and trust. EY research highlights that rising energy costs and growing customer expectations are putting pressure on utilities to deliver clearer communication, greater transparency, and proactive, AI-enabled support that helps customers better understand and manage their energy expenses.5


At the same time,[AI-enabled utility customer experience](https://www.opentext.com/media/point-of-view/total-experience-reimagined-for-energy-and-resources-pov-en.pdf) can make interactions more proactive and personalized. Customer Service Agents could bring together billing, service, outage, and interaction histories. Billing Explanation Agents could translate complex charges into plain language.[Outage Communication Agents](https://www.opentext.com/products/customer-communications-management) could deliver timely, location-specific updates across channels.


Efficiency alone will not define success. Utilities will need to improve customer satisfaction, trust, and affordability while preserving access to people for complex or sensitive situations. As infrastructure investment grows, customers and regulators will expect clear explanations of what is changing, why it is needed, and how it affects bills.


## **Trusted context turns AI into action**


The common thread is trusted context and connected data. Leaders will target high-friction processes, connect authoritative information, and establish clear decision rights and human oversight. They will also need to[design and orchestrate agents at scale, engineered for security](https://www.opentext.com/aviator-ai/aviator-studio) .[Sovereign private cloud](https://www.opentext.com/sovereign-ai-cloud) will become increasingly important as Energy and Resources companies navigate a complex landscape of data residency laws, cybersecurity regulations, and operational requirements. Organizations with data-residency and operational-control requirements should also evaluate sovereign private cloud options for sensitive data and AI workloads.
